system.name: FunCoder
system.one_liner: A code-generation framework that recursively splits a problem into sub-functions and picks the best composed implementation by functional consensus.

content.variant_note: left-to-right flow split by a dash-dot line into divide and conquer halves; sub-functions pass through recursive FunCoder frames and rejoin at a sampling-and-consensus stage; a legend and a six-step tree strip sit underneath
content.argues: Dividing a problem into sub-functions recursively and choosing among sampled compositions by functional consensus yields the final solution; the tree strip shows how the hierarchy grows and collapses.
content.subject: problem function divided into sub-functions, solved recursively, sampled and voted into a final function, plus a six-step tree example

elements.name: FUNCODER ( f(x) )
elements.role: entry point: takes the problem as a function signature f(x)
elements.drawn_as: white card with soft shadow, bold small-caps title and a dashed blue pill holding f(x)

elements.name: f'(x) =
elements.role: partially implemented function whose body refers to the unimplemented sub-functions g(y) and h(z)
elements.drawn_as: blue-outlined white card with a skeleton of grey and coloured bars standing for code lines, two dashed slots at the bottom

elements.name: g(y)
elements.role: unimplemented sub-function branched off f'(x), handed to FunCoder

elements.name: h(z)
elements.role: second unimplemented sub-function, handed to FunCoder

elements.name: FUNCODER (two frames)
elements.role: the same procedure applied recursively to each sub-function
elements.drawn_as: grey rounded frame with the small-caps title on its top edge, holding three pills: outlined, grey, filled

elements.name: g*(y)
elements.role: solved sub-function g that the samples are built on

elements.name: h*(z)
elements.role: solved sub-function h that the samples are built on

elements.name: Sampled Implementations
elements.role: k candidate implementations f'(1) ... f'(k) written against the solved children
elements.drawn_as: blue-outlined white card listing f'(1), f'(2), vertical dots, f'(k-1), f'(k) in a staggered two-column layout

elements.name: Possible Inputs
elements.role: input vector X = (x1, x2, ..., xm) on which the candidates are run
elements.drawn_as: column vector in large brackets with a caption below

elements.name: Functional Consensus
elements.role: compares candidates by their behaviour on possible inputs; the one sharing maximal similarity is kept
elements.drawn_as: plain title above a shadowed cell matrix (listed under pictures)

elements.name: f*(x) =
elements.role: final solution: the consensus implementation combined with the solved children
elements.drawn_as: blue-outlined card with a code skeleton and the solved pills g*(y), h*(z) inside

elements.name: divide | conquer
elements.role: names the two halves of the method
elements.drawn_as: grey words with faint arrows pointing outward from a dash-dot vertical line

elements.name: Legends
elements.role: key for three states of a function: Problem f(x), Partially Implemented f'(x), Reached Consensus f*(x)
elements.drawn_as: framed box with three pink pills: dashed, solid outline, filled

elements.name: Example
elements.role: one dependency tree redrawn after each divide or conquer step
elements.drawn_as: framed strip with six small trees chained by double-line arrows

elements.name: tree snapshots Divide(a) ... Conquer(A)
elements.role: state of the function tree after each step
elements.drawn_as: circles A-E with blue outline for solved nodes, dotted circles a-e for pending nodes

lessons.what_to_learn: Give one object three states by outline style (dashed, solid, filled), define them once in a small legend, reuse the coding on every card and again in a snapshot strip, so a recursive method can be read at both the flow level and the toy-example level.
lessons.suits: recursive or hierarchical methods (decomposition, tree search, sub-goal agents) where one object changes state step by step.

sections: method paragraph that introduces FunCoder (p.4, listed under Abstract in the index)
evidence: FUNCODER recursively branches off sub-functions as smaller goals during code generation, represented by a tree hierarchy.
Functional consensus is calculated by evaluating candidates on possible inputs.
re-composites sub-functions, and selects the best using functional consensus (right)

summary: FunCoder is a code-generation framework that recursively branches sub-functions off a problem function (divide) and then picks the best composed implementation by functional consensus (conquer). The figure is a left-to-right flowgraph in a light grey frame: a title card FUNCODER(f(x)) feeds a partially implemented f'(x) drawn as a code skeleton with dashed teal and pink slots g(y) and h(z); each slot goes through a grey FUNCODER frame to a solved g*(y) or h*(z); k sampled implementations are run on possible inputs X and compared in a blue-and-pink matrix whose winning row is boxed in cyan, giving the final f*(x). Below, a Legends key defines dashed, solid and filled states and an Example strip redraws one dependency tree over six divide and conquer steps.
summary_zh: FunCoder 把问题函数递归拆成子函数，再用功能共识从多个采样实现中选优。图在灰框内自左向右画出拆分、递归求解、共识矩阵投票直到 f*(x)，下方有图例，并用六帧依赖树演示拆分与合并。
